title: Stress test: overflow behavior across every dense layout in the renderer
audience: A Very Long Client Name Holdings International S.A.

slides.kicker: An unusually long kicker label that should still fit on a single line without wrapping badly
slides.heading: A deliberately very long deck title that stresses the two-line assertion headline fitting logic of the cover
slides.subheading: A long supporting subtitle that goes on and on to make sure the cover subhead box shrinks the text rather than colliding with the footer metadata line below it.

slides.heading: Seven items with long two-level content to stress the editorial list

items.title: First item with a fairly long title that could wrap
items.body: And a support line that is also quite long and should be truncated or shrunk gracefully

items.title: Third item about something detailed
items.body: More explanation text here that runs long

items.title: Fifth item with an even longer title to make the row shrink to fit properly

slides.heading: Six cards with long bodies stress the grid and the autofit inside each card

cards.heading: First card with a long heading that wraps
cards.body: A body text that is long enough to test the shrink-to-fit behavior inside a two-row three-column card grid without overflowing the rounded rectangle.

cards.heading: Second card
cards.body: Another moderately long body to fill the card with text and test line spacing at small sizes.

cards.heading: Fourth card heading
cards.body: Yet another long body text used to validate that the text never escapes the card bounds even when dense.

cards.heading: Sixth card with the longest heading of them all to stress the header row
cards.body: Final body text, long enough to wrap a couple of times inside the card.

slides.heading: A six-column ten-row table stresses column widths and row heights

phases.body: Cost tuning, runbook handover, hypercare and the internal enablement academy
